question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
fact: Na comes from natrium, the Latin name for sodium.

question: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
fact: Fe comes from ferrum, the Latin word for iron.

question: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
fact: Air is about 78% nitrogen and only 21% oxygen.

question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
fact: A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.

question: Which is the hottest planet in our solar system?
fact: Venus's thick carbon dioxide air traps heat, so it beats Mercury.

question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
fact: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

question: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
fact: The Andromeda galaxy is on course to merge with ours in billions of years.

question: What is the chemical formula of table salt?
fact: Salt is sodium chloride, made of two elements that are dangerous alone.

question: Which blood type can be given to almost anyone as red blood cells?
fact: AB positive people can receive red cells from any blood type.

question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
fact: An adult's skin weighs several kilograms.

question: Which organ produces insulin?
fact: Insulin was first used to treat a person with diabetes in 1922.

question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
fact: Your heart beats roughly 100,000 times every day.

question: Where in the human body is the smallest bone?
fact: The stapes in the middle ear is only about 3 mm long.

question: Which vitamin does your skin make when exposed to sunlight?
fact: Sailors got scurvy from a lack of vitamin C, not D.

question: About how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
fact: Light could circle the Earth about 7.5 times in one second.

question: Who developed the theory of general relativity?
fact: Einstein's Nobel Prize was for the photoelectric effect, not relativity.

question: Who wrote 'On the Origin of Species' about evolution by natural selection?
fact: Alfred Russel Wallace came up with the same idea independently.

question: Gregor Mendel discovered the rules of heredity by growing which plant?
fact: Mendel was a monk, and his work was ignored until around 1900.

question: Which scientist gave his name to the heating process that makes milk safe?
fact: Pasteur also developed the first vaccine against rabies, in 1885.

question: Edward Jenner made the first vaccine against which disease?
fact: Smallpox was declared wiped out worldwide in 1980.

question: What is the pH of pure water at room temperature?
fact: Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline.

question: Which element has atomic number 1?
fact: Hydrogen makes up about three quarters of the normal matter in the universe.

question: Which gas glows red-orange in classic advertising signs?
fact: Many other 'neon' colours actually come from argon or coated tubes.

question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
fact: Gallium melts at about 30 C, so it can melt in your hand.

question: What does DNA stand for?
fact: Unwound, the DNA in one human cell would be about 2 m long.

question: Which pair first described the double helix structure of DNA in 1953?
fact: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray image was key to the discovery.

question: Which layer of the atmosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful UV rays?
fact: The 1987 Montreal Protocol banned the chemicals that damaged it.

question: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
fact: It is named after the German physicist Georg Ohm.

question: What is the unit of force?
fact: One newton is roughly the weight of a small apple.

question: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
fact: Newton realised the force that drops apples also holds the Moon in orbit.

question: What is the most abundant element in Earth's crust?
fact: Oxygen makes up nearly half the crust's mass, locked inside rocks.

question: What is the dense centre of an atom called?
fact: An atom is almost entirely empty space around a tiny nucleus.

question: Which particle in an atom has a negative charge?
fact: Neutrons have no charge at all, as their name suggests.

question: Roughly how long does the Moon take to orbit the Earth once?
fact: The Moon spins once per orbit, so it always shows us the same face.

question: What mainly causes the ocean tides on Earth?
fact: When Sun and Moon line up, their pull adds up to make spring tides.

question: Which planet has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot?
fact: The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than the whole Earth.

question: Which former planet was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
fact: Pluto is smaller than Earth's Moon.

question: What is the most common type of star in our galaxy?
fact: Red dwarfs live so long that none has yet burned out in the universe's lifetime.

question: Which star is the closest to our Sun?
fact: Its light takes about 4.2 years to reach us.

question: Which is the brightest star in the night sky?
fact: Polaris, the North Star, is only around the 50th brightest star.

question: In which part of a plant cell does photosynthesis happen?
fact: Chlorophyll reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.

question: What do honeybees collect from flowers to make honey?
fact: Honey found in ancient Egyptian tombs was reportedly still edible.

question: Which kind of tree grows the tallest?
fact: Coast redwoods in California can grow taller than 110 m.

question: What type of rock forms when lava or magma cools?
fact: Granite is igneous rock that cooled slowly deep underground.

question: Which instrument records earthquakes?
fact: An anemometer measures wind speed and a hygrometer measures humidity.

question: Which instrument measures air pressure?
fact: Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643.

question: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same number?
fact: Minus 40 is minus 40, whichever of the two scales you use.

question: Absolute zero is closest to which temperature in Celsius?
fact: Absolute zero is -273.15 C; -459 is its value in Fahrenheit.

question: Which gas is the Sun mostly made of?
fact: The Sun fuses roughly 600 million tonnes of hydrogen every second.

question: Which coloured part of the eye controls how much light gets in?
fact: The pupil is simply the hole in the middle of the iris.

question: What does ISS stand for in space travel?
fact: The ISS circles the Earth about every 90 minutes.

question: What was the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth?
fact: Sputnik launched in 1957 and beeped radio signals for about three weeks.

question: Who was the first human to travel into space?
fact: Gagarin orbited Earth once in 1961, in about 108 minutes.

question: Who was the first woman to travel into space?
fact: Tereshkova flew solo in 1963 and orbited Earth 48 times.

question: Which planet has the shortest day?
fact: Jupiter spins so fast that a day there lasts under 10 hours.

question: What do we call a named pattern of stars in the night sky?
fact: Astronomers officially recognise 88 constellations.

question: Which gas makes up most of the atmosphere of Mars?
fact: Mars's air is only about 1% as thick as Earth's.

question: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
fact: Infrared, just beyond red, is what we feel as heat.

question: What kind of energy is stored in a stretched rubber band?
fact: Let go, and the stored energy turns into motion: kinetic energy.

question: What is normal human body temperature in Celsius, roughly?
fact: Body temperature naturally rises and falls a little through the day.

question: What do red blood cells carry around the body?
fact: Human red blood cells have no nucleus, leaving more room for oxygen.

question: Who wrote the three laws of motion?
fact: Newton also ran England's Royal Mint and hunted down coin forgers.

question: Who showed that planets move around the Sun in ellipses, not circles?
fact: Kepler worked from Tycho Brahe's very careful observations.

question: Who published a Sun-centred model of the solar system in 1543?
fact: Ptolemy's older model had put the Earth at the centre.

question: Diamonds and graphite are both made of which element?
fact: Pencil 'lead' is actually graphite, not lead.

question: Which mineral, found in milk, is vital for strong bones?
fact: About 99% of the body's calcium is stored in bones and teeth.

question: What is the scientific study of fungi called?
fact: Fungi are more closely related to animals than to plants.

question: Which tall cloud type brings thunderstorms?
fact: Cumulonimbus clouds can tower more than 10 km high.

question: Through which of these does sound travel fastest?
fact: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum at all.

question: Bamboo belongs to which plant family?
fact: Some bamboo species can grow almost a metre in a single day.
